question: Which sales, yield or additional-cost thresholds could change the result of the four frozen dated Tsiri programs, and when is more demand alone insufficient?
baseline: Each context21 author-exported program and scenario, existing RW flights retained; unchanged dated supply and flight costs.
money_basis: Conditional carrier net yield and author cost basis; no matched contracts or actual profit claim.
null_policy: Unknown full-budget costs stay NULL. Zero extra burden is explicitly an optimistic relaxation, not an estimate.

experiments.change: Scale new and foregone old fares together at fixed author sales and flight/pax cost
experiments.effect: Solve exact zero-contribution fare multiplier; distinguish new-only repricing.
experiments.refusal: Cannot call fare multiplier a demand forecast or assume unchanged sales at changed prices.

experiments.change: Remove every demand cap and own migration, allow all nominal seats sold on existing itineraries
experiments.effect: Compute a certified optimistic contribution upper bound using per-leg local fares and itinerary incidence.
experiments.refusal: Negative bound excludes only this dated supply at these fares/costs; it does not exclude every network, cost change or future aircraft.

experiments.change: Add per-allocated-tail and new-base weekly costs as explicit unknown parameters
experiments.effect: Show exact affine pairwise boundaries; future fixed resource costs charged only where incremental.
experiments.refusal: No winner across different case-compliance levels or unobserved budgets; lower loss is not launch.

experiments.change: Compute donor and retained-own-sales effects by full baseline/candidate states
experiments.effect: Demonstrate algebraic equality to incremental formula and detect double count.
experiments.refusal: Illustrative numeric fixtures do not select an actual donor or actual replacement.

experiments.change: Separate operating result, deposits and dated cash flows
experiments.effect: Reconcile positive result with earlier funding need without expensing working capital twice.
experiments.refusal: Illustrative fixture is not a company cash forecast.

supply_certificate: For each leg l, lambda_l = local_fare_l - passenger_cost_l. Verify lambda>=0 and sum(lambda_l for l in itinerary)>=through_fare - itinerary_pax_cost. Then sum(capacity_l*lambda_l)-flight_cost is an upper bound. Filling every leg with local journeys attains it in the relaxed model.
comparability: All four Tsiri programs share the source week and 4+1 maximum. This does not yet make Anastasia annual programs numerically comparable.
